newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Most Russian energy firms insolvent - oil minister.
newsitem.headline: Most Russian energy firms insolvent - oil minister.

text.p: Ninety percent of Russia's energy companies are insolvent, Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov was quoted by Prime-Tass news agency as saying on Wednesday.

Rodionov, speaking at a ministry session on the performance of oil, gas, electricity, coal and other energy companies over 1996, blamed a non-payments crisis, in which consumer debts to energy firms for unpaid supplies nearly doubled over 1996 to 356 trillion roubles.
Natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom and national electricity utility Unified Energy System (UES) were owed 78 percent of the total but had the least leeway to cut supplies to non-payers.
Total investments in the oil sector fell one-quarter year-on-year and slipped over five percent in the gas sector, Prime-Tass said, without naming numbers or investment sources.
Rodionov, quoted by Interfax news agency, said he was satisfied with output last year at energy companies but said firms had failed to emerge from financial crisis.
Oil firms for the first time appear to have turned the tide against a decade of steep output declines.

Rodionov said total Russian oil and gas condensate output last year was about 301 million tonnes (6.02 million barrels per day, or bpd), a drop of 5.8 million tonnes (116,000 bpd) on 1995's level and the smallest decline yet.
State Statistics Committee figures earlier put 1996 output down two percent on 1995 to 293 million tonnes (around 5.86 million bpd).
Rodionov said 1996 gas output rose six billion cubic metres, or bcm, to 601.5 billion cubic metres.
Electricity output slipped 12.5 billion kilowatt hours to 847.5 billion kilowatt hours.
